question: The words Socialist, Secular and Integrity were added in the preamble of Indian Constitution by which amendment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The words "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity" were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is also known as the **Mini-Constitution** because of the extensive changes it made to the Constitution.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the Emergency period under the prime ministership of **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The 42nd Amendment aimed at giving the Indian Constitution a socialist and secular character, reflecting the objectives of social justice and equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socialist**:

 
 
• The term "Socialist" was added to emphasize India's commitment to social and economic equality.
 
• It signifies that wealth should be distributed in a manner that serves the common good.
 
• It aims to reduce the gap between the rich and the poor through government intervention in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Secular**:
 
 
• The term "Secular" signifies that India does not have an official state religion.
 
• It ensures that all religions are treated equally and that the state does not favor or discriminate against any religion.
 
• This term reinforces the commitment to religious freedom and tolerance.
 
 
 
• **Integrity**:
 
 
• The word "Integrity" was added to emphasize the unity and cohesiveness of the nation.
 
• It signifies the importance of maintaining the territorial and communal integrity of the country.
 
• This addition underscores the commitment to the unity of the nation amidst its diverse cultures and populations.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**:
 
 
• Also known as the Mini-Constitution due to the extensive changes it made.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period (1975-1977) under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• It brought about significant changes in the Constitution, including the addition of fundamental duties and changes to the Preamble and the Seventh Schedule.
 
• Many of its provisions were later undone or modified by subsequent amendments, particularly the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
